evidence.exact_quote: UI command catalog compatibility preserves existing GUI command names and shortcuts while path/context discovery routes through DiscoveryService. Quick Open, command palette fuzzy file search, Search path narrowing, Assistant Chat file mentions, File Manager type-ahead, Planning Wizard source picker, and PRD Builder source picker do not require a parallel cmd.discovery.* GUI command family. cmd.search.* remains Search/content command canon, and DiscoveryService is the path/context routing substrate for compatible surfaces. Discovery/frecency reset controls require storage/search settings owner reconciliation before adding new command IDs.

items.impact: Frecency or discovery-reset controls cannot be registered deterministically until storage/search ownership and the canonical command namespace are adjudicated.
items.statement: UCC-099 closes compatibility for existing search and picker surfaces, but explicitly leaves discovery/frecency reset command ownership unresolved and therefore leaves new reset IDs to builder discretion.
items.title: Discovery reset command ownership remains unresolved

items.impact: Implementers can invent incompatible IDs, payloads, terminal results, and stale-state recovery behavior for the many History actions, making wiring and negative-path fixtures non-falsifiable.
items.statement: UCC-100 enumerates a large History action surface and strong stale/currentness prohibitions, but it does not assign action-level cmd.* IDs or closed payload, result, error, and recovery contracts within the unit.
items.title: History wrappers lack action-level command contracts

items.impact: The GUI is forbidden from overstating model perception and remembered permission state must remain inspectable and revocable.
items.statement: UCC-101 explicitly closes two high-risk trust boundaries: bridge-derived answers cannot masquerade as direct image perception, and remembered always-accept rules cannot be hidden or irrevocable.

items.statement: UCC-107 strongly limits dev-preview authority, but 'unless explicitly configured' does not identify the configuration owner, build-time versus runtime mechanism, permission gate, receipt, or production acceptance oracle.
items.title: Dev-preview production enablement is under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: Every command in this addendum returns the `UICommandResponse` envelope from `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`. The field-level response minimum is `schema_version`, `dispatch_id`, `command_id`, `ack_status`, `result_status?`, `error?`, `event_refs[]?`, `receipt_ref?`, and `ts`. Error codes are closed to `invalid_route`, `unknown_command`, `invalid_args`, `permission_denied`, `blocked_state_required`, `stale_projection`, `handler_unavailable`, and `internal_error`. Commands that intentionally emit no persisted domain event still record a dispatch receipt or route/open disposition and must not fabricate `*.command_applied` events.

items.impact: Command success, error, and no-domain-event dispositions have a shared falsifiable envelope and cannot be represented by fabricated generic success events.
items.statement: UCC-108 closes the shared response and receipt baseline with exact fields, a closed error set, explicit receipts for no-event commands, and a categorical ban on fabricated command_applied events.
items.title: FABLE response and receipt baseline is closed

evidence.exact_quote: - Timestamp, run-only, thread-only, or tier-only payloads may narrow filters but cannot satisfy the primary Usage route identity when usage_event_ref is available.

items.impact: Legacy or partial callers without usage_event_ref can resolve the same payload to different Usage subjects, or display a narrowed filter as if it were canonical object identity.
items.statement: UCC-109 precisely defines object-first identity when usage_event_ref exists, but does not define precedence, conflict handling, or terminal failure when it is absent and multiple alternative refs disagree.
items.title: Usage fallback identity resolution remains ambiguous

segments.summary: Reviewed UCC-099 through UCC-101 across compatibility routing, History actions, vision provenance, permissions, stale-state behavior, consumers, failure paths, and negative constraints; found unresolved discovery-reset ownership and prose-only History dispatch contracts while confirming explicit vision trust boundaries.

Reviewed Teach, Notifications and Sounds, and DRY settings command units including GUI states, mutation authority, accessibility, destructive behavior, concurrency, recovery, and fixtures; concrete dispatch closure is missing for Teach, delete recovery, and stale DRY writes.

Reviewed onboarding, container-host, dev-preview, planning/build, testing, alias, and FABLE command rows across authority, transitions, payloads, receipts, compatibility, failures, destructive operations, and production boundaries; found unresolved conditional host fields, onboarding transitions, and dev-preview enablement authority.

Reviewed UCC-108 response closure, strict schema overlay, compatibility treatment, and UCC-109 Usage routing identity across exact fields, errors, receipts, legacy aliases, and adversarial partial-identity cases; the shared response baseline is closed but Usage fallback precedence is not.
